docs.title: AstralVessel
docs.text:
AstralVessel is the AstralDeep base with its command-line tools and no graphical interface. One command, astralvessel up, runs a personal node: the backend, and a way to talk to it.

The node is an AstralDeep orchestrator in its personal profile. It stores everything in SQLite in a Docker volume, joins the owner's mesh, and serves A2A and MCP. Beside it runs the executor, which checks a ticket before a sandbox runs a tool, and an optional egress for model calls.

The AstralDeep app is a separate installation. It carries everything here and adds the interface.

docs.title: What runs
docs.text:
• The node. An AstralDeep image configured for one owner, with no PostgreSQL. See How it works.
  • The executor. A service in front of each agent's sandbox. It verifies the ticket, the action it covers and the tool definition, then forwards the call. See The executor.
  • A sandbox per agent. No network, no secrets of the node, a read-only root and read-only data. Each call is confined with Landlock and seccomp. See Isolation and probes.
  • An egress. Optional. It holds a model key so the node never does. See The egress.

docs.title: Where to start
docs.text: If you want to Read Install and start a node Quickstart Add the node from the AstralDeep app Pairing Move from 0.6.0 Migration from 0.6.0 Look up a setting Configuration tables Write tools for an agent The agent folder Judge the risk Threat model

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Linux 6.12 or newer with Landlock ABI 6, or Docker Desktop on Apple silicon. See Platform support.
  • Docker with Compose.
  • Python 3.11 or newer for the astralvessel command.
  • An AstralDeep node image built with the kernel binding. See Quickstart.

AstralVessel is licensed under Apache 2.0.

AstralVessel becomes the base's headless installation. See Migration from 0.6.0.

  • astralvessel up runs a personal AstralDeep node on SQLite in a named volume, with no PostgreSQL.
  • Added the executor, which verifies tickets before a sandbox runs a tool, and pair, conformance, ask and chat against the node.
  • The sandbox and egress containers are kept. The probes now check the node, the executor and the egress.
  • The executor image build needs the pinned kernel wheel and checks its sha256. A missing kernel gives executor.no_kernel.
  • Each agent has its own executor token, in .generated/executor-agents.json. The operator token lists and pairs only.
  • The executor derives a call's owner and workspace from the deployment and the verified ticket, never from the request.
  • Spent ticket ids persist across an executor restart.
  • Removed the agent loop, the A2A server, identities, history, service tools, web tools and search.

• Four-command setup. astralvessel up writes deployment.toml and a private .env when there is none (asking for agent folders, model URL, key and model, or taking them as options; env:NAME keeps the key out of every file), starts the deployment, waits until every sandbox is confined, runs the isolation probes and tests the model. --example sets up the example agent, which now ships in the package.
  • astralvessel check runs the isolation probes against every agent of any deployment; they ship in the package and replace deploy/verify-isolation.sh.
  • astralvessel chat (saved, resumable chats through the history store) and astralvessel ask (one turn), run in a short-lived container on the internal front network; astralvessel down stops a deployment.
  • An optional model per agent in deployment.toml, overriding the agent folder's.
  • The conformance suite is removed. Its checks that the tests did not already make are now in the test suite.
  • The vessel's address is reserved. Containers that join front (applications, chat, ask) now get addresses only from the upper half of front_subnet, so none can take the vessel's address while it is stopped. front_address must be in the lower half (the default .10 is), and front_subnet must be a /28 or larger. The next up (or deploy plus docker compose up) recreates an existing deployment's front network: stop applications attached to it first, and start them again afterward.
  • macOS with Docker Desktop on Apple silicon is supported, after the isolation probes passed there.
  • The documentation site now updates when a release is published, not on every change to main.
  • tool_error is no longer a turn status; it was reserved and never produced. A failed tool call never ends a turn.
  • turn.finished is documented as always carrying files, [] when none, with a regression test.

• A workspace per turn that its tool calls share, deleted when the turn ends.
  • Files from tools (PNG, SVG, CSV, PDF) through $VESSEL_OUTBOX, checked twice and streamed as A2A artifacts.
  • [vessel] project for several deployments on one host.
  • CI (lint, tests on Python 3.11 and 3.12, isolation probes on a running deployment), Dependabot, and a release workflow that publishes multi-architecture images to GHCR and the package to PyPI.
  • The model endpoint is required. [egress] upstream_url has no default; set it to an http:// or https:// URL or to env:NAME. The example deployment reads it from VESSEL_UPSTREAM_MODEL_URL.
  • Disk limits per turn and per user. turn_disk and user_disk in [agents.sandbox] (by default a quarter and half of scratch). No file may outgrow the turn's limit; each file or folder also counts 1 KB; files deleted but still open count. A turn over either limit has its calls stopped and its workspace emptied. One new isolation probe.
  • Calls stay in their session. seccomp blocks setsid and setpgid, and each call may hold at most 4,096 open files.
  • Issuer key files work in the generated deployment. A jwks_file is mounted into the vessel, a missing one is refused when the deployment loads, and changing its contents recreates the vessel on the next up -d.
  • The conformance checks accept the file event.
  • A documentation site, built with MkDocs and published to GitHub Pages.
  • The isolation probes now number 43.

• Verified-token callers: an issuer allowlist with audience, expiry, authorized party and asymmetric signature checks; owners keyed by issuer and subject.
  • Per-call scope narrowing through token scopes or X-Vessel-Scopes.
  • Structured skill calls in the shape Astral sends to external agents.
  • Web search through a private SearXNG container, with failed searches reported as errors.
  • A token on the egress model passthrough, so only the vessel can spend the key.
  • A turn survives tool arguments that are not JSON.
  • The vessel and sandboxes are recreated when an agent's manifest, tools or the deployment change, and a sandbox is served only if it loaded the same tools as the vessel.

• Service tools answered by the application over HTTP, with credentials held by the vessel.
  • Image input for agents whose model accepts images.
  • Per-agent sandbox images built from a Dockerfile in the agent folder.
  • Briefings reloaded on every turn, and prompt_append so one folder can serve as several agents.
  • volume:NAME mount sources.

• One vessel serving many agents, each with its own sandbox, card and A2A address.
  • deployment.toml, per-app keys, and Compose generated by astralvessel deploy.
  • Application-owned history, with transcripts streamed in OpenAI chat format.
  • Per-call confinement with Landlock and seccomp.
• The first harness: the agent loop, sandbox, egress, conformance checks and isolation probes.

docs.title: The node image is not on this machine
docs.text: up stops with the image name. Build or pull a node image with the kernel binding and tag it with that name, or set image in [node].

docs.title: The node never becomes ready
docs.text: Run docker compose -f compose.generated.yml logs node. The node exits with code 78 when a secret, the issuer or the data directory is missing or unwritable. Production is the default, so an http issuer needs ASTRAL_ENV = "development" under [node.environment]. Use that only for development.

docs.title: A sandbox exits at start
docs.text:
this kernel lacks Landlock ABI 6

The host kernel is too old. See Platform support.

docs.title: The probes fail
docs.text: check prints the failing check by container. A failure in a sandbox probe means isolation does not hold on this host. Do not use the deployment until it passes.

docs.title: pair says the node refused the owner token
docs.text: The token must be current, from the issuer in [owner], for the one owner the node serves. A token for another owner gets HTTP 403.

docs.title: pair --executor says the node has not joined
docs.text: The executor waits for the node's mailbox, which exists only after the node has joined the owner's mesh. Pair the node first.

docs.title: Every call is refused with executor.no_kernel
docs.text: The kernel binding does not import in the executor's image. An image built here always has it, because the build fails without the pinned wheel and mailbox. Rebuild from this checkout with [executor] kernel_artifacts set, or use the released image.

docs.title: The image build says it needs the pinned kernel wheel
docs.text: The build checks the wheel and mailbox sha256 values against config/kernel-binding.json and stops if either artifact is missing or differs. Point [executor] kernel_artifacts at the folder that holds astral_kernel-<version>-py3-none-manylinux_2_36_<arch>.whl and astral-mailbox-linux-<arch>. The binding pins only the architectures it lists.

docs.title: A call is refused with a ticket.* code
docs.text: The ticket did not verify. The code says why, for example ticket.expired, ticket.mesh_mismatch or gate.mesh_stopped. The executor runs nothing in that case.

docs.title: The agent folder
docs.text: An agent is a folder. This page shows its layout and walks through writing a small agent from scratch.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
my-agent/
├── vessel.toml          # required: the manifest
├── tools/               # optional: declared tools
│   ├── lookup.toml
│   └── lookup.py
└── sandbox.Dockerfile   # optional: extra software for the sandbox
File Required What it does vessel.toml yes Names the agent, lists its tools, and says what data and limits its sandbox needs. See vessel.toml. Declared tool files no One TOML file per tool, listed in [tools] declared. Paths are relative to the folder and must stay inside it. See Declared tools. A sandbox Dockerfile no Named by [sandbox] dockerfile, built FROM astralvessel. See Extra software.

The manifest lists everything the agent has. A tool that is not listed does not exist for the executor.

The sandbox mounts the folder read-only at /agent, and tool calls may read it, so keep secrets out of it.

docs.title: Write an agent
docs.text:
This agent answers questions about a folder of Markdown notes.

  1. Create the folder:

    mkdir -p agents/notes

  2. Write the manifest, agents/notes/vessel.toml:

    [agent]
name = "notes"
description = "Answers questions from a folder of notes."

[tools]
builtin = ["read", "grep", "glob", "list"]

[sandbox]
workdir = "/data"
mounts = [{ source = "notes", target = "/data" }]

    The mount says the agent needs data at /data. source is only a label here; the deployment decides what is actually mounted.

  3. Grant it in deployment.toml:

    [egress]
upstream_url = "https://api.example.com/v1"

[[agents]]
id = "notes"
package = "agents/notes"
[agents.sandbox]
mounts = [{ target = "/data", source = "/srv/notes" }]

[[apps]]
name = "web"
key_sha256 = "env:WEB_APP_KEY_SHA256"
agents = ["notes"]

    package is relative to the deployment file. The grant's target must match the manifest's mount target.

  4. Deploy it:

    astralvessel deploy deployment.toml
docker compose -f compose.generated.yml --env-file .env up -d --build

    deploy refuses a deployment whose grants do not match what the agent declares, so a missing or extra mount fails here, not at run time.

docs.title: One folder, several agents
docs.text: A deployment can list the same folder under several agent ids. Each id gets its own sandbox.

docs.title: Check a folder before deploying
docs.text:
load_package parses and validates a folder the same way the executor does:

python -c 'from astralvessel.manifest import load_package; p = load_package("agents/notes"); print(p.tool_scopes())'

It raises an error naming the first problem: an unknown setting, an unknown built-in tool, a declared tool outside the folder, or two tools with the same name.

docs.title: Built-in tools
docs.text:
AstralVessel ships seven tools an agent can list in [tools] builtin. This page gives each one's arguments, limits and where it runs.

[tools]
builtin = ["read", "grep", "glob", "list", "bash"]
Tool Runs in Scope Does read sandbox server tools:files Reads a text file as numbered lines grep sandbox, confined tools:search Searches file contents with a regular expression glob sandbox server tools:files Finds files by path pattern list sandbox server tools:files Lists a directory bash sandbox, confined tools:execute Runs a shell command

Paths may be absolute or relative to the agent's workdir. The file tools can reach only the system directories, the agent folder (/agent), the workdir, the mounted data and the turn's workspace; anything else is refused as outside the agent's data. read, glob and list check where an opened path really points, so a symbolic link cannot lead them outside.

docs.title: read
docs.text:
Argument Type Default Notes path string required A file offset integer 1 First line to return limit integer 400 Lines to return, at most 2,000

Returns lines as N<tab>text. A line longer than 4,000 characters is cut and marked [line truncated]. When more lines follow, the last line says which offset to continue with.

docs.title: grep
docs.text:
Argument Type Default Notes pattern string required ripgrep regular expression syntax path string the workdir File or directory glob string Only files matching this glob, such as *.md ignore_case boolean false max_results integer 100 At most 1,000

Returns path:line:text lines, each cut at 400 columns. Uses rg when the image has it (the AstralVessel image does), and grep -rnE otherwise. Runs as a confined process, like bash.

docs.title: glob
docs.text:
Argument Type Default Notes pattern string required Relative, without ..; a pattern with no /, such as *.md, searches the whole tree path string the workdir Directory to search from max_results integer 200 At most 2,000

Stops after the agent's tool_timeout_seconds and says so.

docs.title: list
docs.text:
Argument Type Default path string the workdir

Lists directories first, each with a trailing /, then files, up to 500 entries.

docs.title: bash
docs.text:
Argument Type Default command string required

Runs /bin/sh -c <command> in the workdir as a confined process and returns the combined output followed by [exit code N]. A non-zero exit marks the result as an error. The same confinement, environment and output limits as declared tools apply. bash gives the caller a general-purpose shell over everything the agent can read, so it carries the strongest scope.

docs.title: Declared tools
docs.text: A declared tool is a command the agent's sandbox runs when it is called. This page covers the tool file, how arguments reach the command, and what comes back.

docs.title: Write a tool
docs.text:
A tool is a TOML file in the agent folder, listed in vessel.toml:

# vessel.toml
[tools]
declared = ["tools/species.toml"]

# tools/species.toml
name = "species"
description = "List every species in the guide with its family, habitats and length, as JSON."
command = ["python3", "{package}/tools/species.py"]
scope = "tools:read"

[parameters]
type = "object"
[parameters.properties.habitat]
type = "string"
description = "Only species with this habitat (optional)"

# Prints every species page's frontmatter as JSON, optionally filtered by habitat; reads the request from stdin.
import json
import pathlib
import sys

request = json.load(sys.stdin)
wanted = (request.get("habitat") or "").lower()
rows = []
for page in sorted(pathlib.Path("species").glob("*.md")):
    head = page.read_text().split("---")[1]
    fields = dict(line.split(": ", 1) for line in head.strip().splitlines())
    habitats = [h.strip() for h in fields["habitat"].strip("[]").split(",")]
    if wanted and wanted not in habitats:
        continue
    rows.append({"page": page.name, "name": fields["name"], "family": fields["family"],
                 "habitat": habitats, "length_cm": int(fields["length_cm"])})
print(json.dumps(rows, indent=1))

The command runs with the agent's workdir as its current directory, so species above is /data/species when workdir = "/data".

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Key Default Meaning name required Lowercase letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter, up to 63 characters. May not repeat a built-in tool or another declared tool. description required What the caller gets to decide when to call it. command The argument vector to run. {package} is replaced with the agent folder's path in the sandbox (/agent). parameters {"type": "object", "properties": {}} A JSON Schema for the arguments, kept as the tool's input schema. input "json-stdin" How arguments reach the command: json-stdin or args. timeout_seconds the agent's tool_timeout_seconds This tool's time limit. scope "tools:read" Its permission scope.

docs.title: How arguments arrive
docs.text:
With input = "json-stdin" (the default), the command receives the call's arguments as one JSON object on standard input.

With input = "args", each argument becomes a --name=value flag appended to the command, and standard input is empty. Only names declared under parameters.properties are accepted; a call with any other argument is refused before the command runs, so a caller cannot add flags of its own.

# tools/word_count.toml
name = "word_count"
description = "Count the words in one file."
command = ["python3", "{package}/tools/word_count.py"]
input = "args"
[parameters]
type = "object"
required = ["path"]
[parameters.properties.path]
type = "string"

# tools/word_count.py: called as word_count.py --path=notes/a.md
import argparse
import pathlib

parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
parser.add_argument("--path", required=True)
print(len(pathlib.Path(parser.parse_args().path).read_text().split()))

Values are passed with Python's str(), so a boolean arrives as True or False and a list as its Python form. Prefer json-stdin for anything beyond plain strings and numbers.

The executor refuses arguments that are not a JSON object.

docs.title: What the caller gets
docs.text:
The command's standard output and standard error, combined, are the result. An exit status other than zero marks the call as an error. Empty output becomes [exit code N].

Output is cut to the agent's tool_output_chars, with a note saying how much was dropped. A call that runs past timeout_seconds (or tool_timeout_seconds) has its process group killed and returns [timed out after N s]. The fixed output caps are in Limits.

docs.title: Where it runs
docs.text:
Each call runs in the agent's sandbox as its own confined process:

  • It can read the system directories, the agent folder (/agent), the workdir and the mounted data, and write only the turn's workspace ($TMPDIR, also $HOME).
  • It has no network, cannot see or signal other processes, cannot make socket files, and cannot use shared memory or message queues.
  • Its environment holds only PATH, LANG, HOME, TMPDIR and VESSEL_OUTBOX, never a secret.
  • It cannot start a new session or process group (setsid and setpgid are blocked), so processes it leaves running in the background are killed with it. It may hold at most 4,096 open files, and may not write a single file larger than the turn's disk limit (see Disk limits).

A tool that needs software beyond the base image ships a sandbox Dockerfile. A tool can return files by writing them into $VESSEL_OUTBOX; see Workspaces and files.

docs.title: Test a tool locally
docs.text:
Run the script the way the sandbox does, with the arguments on standard input and the workdir as the current directory:

cd examples/sample-data
echo '{"habitat": "rivers"}' | python3 ../field-guide/tools/species.py

docs.title: vessel.toml
docs.text: vessel.toml is an agent's manifest: what it is called, which tools it has, and what its sandbox needs. Unknown keys are refused. Types, defaults and constraints for every key are generated from the code in Configuration tables.

docs.title: A complete example
docs.text:
[agent]
name = "field-guide"
description = "Answers questions about the birds in a small sample field guide."
version = "0.1.0"


[tools]
builtin = ["read", "grep", "glob", "list", "bash"]
declared = ["tools/species.toml"]

[sandbox]
workdir = "/data"
mounts = [{ source = "guide", target = "/data", read_only = true }]
deadline_seconds = 300
tool_timeout_seconds = 30

[output]
files = ["png", "csv"]

docs.title: [agent]
docs.text:
Key Meaning name Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter, up to 63 characters. Names the agent in the executor's catalog. description One or two sentences. Shown in the executor's catalog. version The agent's version.

The agent's id in deployment.toml is what callers use, not name.

docs.title: [tools]
docs.text: Key Meaning builtin Any of read, grep, glob, list, bash. See Built-in tools. declared Paths to declared tool files, relative to the agent folder. See Declared tools.

docs.title: [sandbox]
docs.text:
Key Meaning workdir The working directory for tool calls, and the base for relative paths. It must exist in the sandbox: set it to one of your mount targets. mounts The data the agent needs, as { source, target, read_only }. target is the path inside the sandbox; source is a label (the deployment chooses the real source). read_only must be true. deadline_seconds How long the sandbox tracks a turn, 5 to 3600 seconds. tool_timeout_seconds Each tool call's time limit, 1 to 600. A declared tool may set its own. tool_output_chars How much of a tool's output the executor returns, 1,000 to 200,000 characters. Longer output is cut with a note saying how much was dropped. dockerfile A Dockerfile in the agent folder for a custom sandbox image.

Every mount needs a matching grant in deployment.toml, and every grant a matching mount. Writable mounts are not supported: each turn writes only to its own workspace.

docs.title: Extra software in the sandbox
docs.text:
An agent whose tools need more than the base image (Python 3.11, ripgrep, a POSIX shell) can ship a Dockerfile in its folder. It must start FROM astralvessel; deploy points that name at the AstralVessel image it uses.

# agents/charts/sandbox.Dockerfile
FROM astralvessel
USER root
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir matplotlib==3.9.2
USER vessel

[sandbox]
dockerfile = "sandbox.Dockerfile"

The base image runs as the unprivileged vessel user; switch back to it after installing. The Dockerfile must be inside the agent folder. Its contents, and every file its COPY and ADD lines bring in from the folder, are part of the agent's profile fingerprint, so editing them marks the sandbox stale until you run deploy and docker compose ... up -d --build.

docs.title: [output]
docs.text: Key Meaning files File types tools may return: any of png, svg, csv, pdf. See Workspaces and files.

docs.title: Permission scopes
docs.text:
Each tool carries one of six permission scopes, weakest first: tools:read, tools:search, tools:files, tools:write, tools:system, tools:execute. The executor's catalog lists each tool's scope and the strongest scope for the agent. The scope also decides the effect kind the ticket is verified for: tools:read and tools:search are outward reads and the rest are outside effects.

Tool Scope read, glob, list tools:files grep tools:search bash tools:execute Declared tools their scope, default tools:read

docs.title: Workspaces and files
docs.text: Each turn gets a scratch directory its tool calls share, and tools can return files to the caller through an outbox inside it. This page covers both, and the disk limits that apply.

docs.title: The turn's workspace
docs.text:
The first sandbox call of a turn creates a workspace, a fresh directory under the sandbox's /tmp. Every confined call of that turn sees it as $TMPDIR and $HOME, and it is the only place a call can write. So one call can save an intermediate result and a later call in the same turn can read it:

# first bash call
grep -l heron /data/species/*.md > "$TMPDIR/hits.txt"
# a later call in the same turn
wc -l < "$TMPDIR/hits.txt"
  • The workspace is deleted when the turn ends, whether it finished, failed, hit its deadline or was cancelled. Calls still running for the turn are stopped first.
  • A call cannot read another turn's workspace, even one for the same user.
  • If the executor cannot tell the sandbox a turn ended, the sandbox stops tracking the turn a minute after the agent's deadline_seconds and removes its workspace on the next call it receives.
  • A call that arrives for a turn that has already ended is refused.
  • The sandbox's /tmp is mounted noexec, so files in the workspace cannot be run directly; run scripts with their interpreter (sh script.sh, python3 script.py).
  • The total size of every workspace in a sandbox is capped by the agent's scratch setting in deployment.toml (default 256m).

docs.title: Disk limits
docs.text:
New in 0.5.0

Per-turn and per-user disk limits.

Inside scratch, the sandbox limits how much one turn and one user may hold, so one turn cannot fill the space other users share:

[[agents]]
id = "field-guide"
package = "../examples/field-guide"
[agents.sandbox]
scratch = "256m"
turn_disk = "64m"    # default: a quarter of scratch
user_disk = "128m"   # default: half of scratch

Sizes use Docker's form: a number with an optional b, k, m or g (powers of 1,024). deploy refuses anything but 0 < turn_disk <= user_disk <= scratch.

Rule Detail Per file No single file a call writes may grow past turn_disk. Per turn The turn's workspace may hold at most turn_disk. Per user All of one user's live turns on this agent together may hold at most user_disk. What counts Allocated blocks (sparse files cannot hide), plus 1 KB for every file or folder, plus files deleted but still held open by the turn's processes. A tree too deep to measure counts as over. When it is checked About twice a second while a call runs, and when it ends. A fast writer can briefly overshoot; scratch stays the hard ceiling. What happens Every call of the turn is stopped, its workspace is emptied, and the call's output names the limit. The turn can go on with an empty workspace.

The sandbox's /tmp also has one inode per KB of scratch.

docs.title: Files from tools
docs.text:
An agent that lists file types can return files to the caller:

[output]
files = ["png", "csv"]   # any of png, svg, csv, pdf

A confined call writes files into $VESSEL_OUTBOX, a folder inside its workspace:

printf 'name,length_cm\nGreat Blue Heron,115\n' > "$VESSEL_OUTBOX/lengths.csv"

After each call the sandbox takes every entry out of the outbox. It keeps a file only if all of these hold:

Check Rule Type A regular file (not a link, folder or pipe) Name Starts with a letter or digit, then letters, digits, ., _ or -, up to 100 characters, ending in a listed extension Content PNG and PDF must start with their signatures; SVG and CSV must be UTF-8 without NUL bytes, and SVG must contain <svg near the start Size At most 4 MB each Count At most 4 per call

The executor checks every file again when it arrives.

docs.title: How files reach the caller
docs.text:
POST /run on the executor returns the kept files in a files list. Each entry has name, media_type and base64 data. The executor does not keep them.

Extension Media type png image/png svg image/svg+xml csv text/csv pdf application/pdf

SVG can carry script

Show an SVG as an <img> or offer it as a download. Never insert it inline into a page.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
astralvessel up turns deployment.toml into a Compose file. Nothing in the running system controls Docker.

Container Networks Holds node front, outside, and egress when a gateway is set The node's data volume with SQLite, its signing key and its mesh keys executor front, and one tools network per agent Its own mesh keys, and the sandbox master token sandbox-<agent> its own tools network, which is internal Nothing of the node egress egress, outside The model key, only when [egress] is set

docs.title: The node
docs.text: The node runs with ASTRAL_NODE_PROFILE=personal. Its data directory is mode 0700 and its database file and keys are mode 0600. It trusts one issuer and one owner. Its A2A endpoint is /a2a and it publishes a descriptor at /api/node/descriptor. Deep's turn loop runs every turn. AstralVessel has no loop of its own.

docs.title: The executor
docs.text:
A tool call for a sandboxed agent goes to the executor with a ticket and the action it covers. The executor refuses unless the ticket verifies against its own copy of the owner's roster. Then it forwards the call to the right sandbox with that sandbox's own token.

The executor is a member of the owner's mesh, so it can verify tickets without asking anyone. The owner adds it the same way as the node. See The executor.

docs.title: The sandboxes
docs.text: A sandbox runs file, shell and declared tools. It has no network route, a read-only root and read-only data. Each call is confined with Landlock and seccomp, so users who share an agent cannot see each other. The per-agent bearer token stays as a second check behind the ticket.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: This guide builds a personal AstralDeep node, installs the AstralVessel command, and checks the running node.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Python 3.11 or newer, Git, and Docker with Buildx and the Compose v2 plugin.
  • A supported sandbox host: Linux x86_64 or arm64 with kernel 6.12 or newer and Landlock ABI 6; or an Apple silicon Mac with Docker Desktop whose Linux VM provides Landlock ABI 6. Docker Desktop 29.5 with a kernel 6.12 VM was checked; older versions may ship an older kernel. Windows with Docker Desktop is unverified. See platform support.
  • An AstralDeep Keycloak issuer and client ID. Use the values configured for the AstralDeep app you use. See realm setup and the relevant Android and iOS client or Windows client guide.

docs.title: 1. Prepare the node build inputs
docs.text:
The AstralVessel 0.7.0 executor image contains the exact, verified Kernel artifacts used to build the matching Deep node image. Use it only to copy those files; it is not the node image and must not be passed to astralvessel up --image.

mkdir astral-install && cd astral-install
docker pull ghcr.io/astraldeep/astralvessel:0.7.0
artifact_container="$(docker create ghcr.io/astraldeep/astralvessel:0.7.0)"
mkdir kernel-artifacts
docker cp "${artifact_container}:/opt/vessel-build/kernel-artifacts/." ./kernel-artifacts/
docker rm "$artifact_container"

docker create does not start the executor. The release image is public; this step needs no registry login.

docs.title: 2. Build the node image
docs.text:
Clone the qualified AstralDeep source and initialize its pinned submodules:

git clone https://github.com/AstralDeep/AstralDeep.git astraldeep
cd astraldeep
git checkout 67519cba8964cb77335642bd7fdb5871f996547a
git submodule update --init --recursive

Build for the machine that will run Docker. The named build context points to the artifacts copied in the previous step:

Linux x86_64Linux arm64 or Apple silicon 
docker build --platform linux/amd64 --build-context kernel-artifacts=../kernel-artifacts -t astralvessel-node:local .

docker build --platform linux/arm64 --build-context kernel-artifacts=../kernel-artifacts -t astralvessel-node:local .

Deep's image build checks the wheel and mailbox against its pinned manifest and fails if either is missing or differs. astralvessel-node:local is the default node image name.

docs.title: 3. Install AstralVessel
docs.text: python3 -m pip install astralvessel==0.7.0

docs.title: 4. Start and check the node
docs.text:
Use your Keycloak realm URL as the issuer and the client ID configured for your AstralDeep app. The example uses astral-mobile:

cd ..
mkdir mynode && cd mynode
astralvessel up --issuer https://keycloak.example/realms/astral --client-id astral-mobile --example

up writes a private deployment file, starts the node and executor, waits for them to become ready, and runs the checks. The node listens on 127.0.0.1:8001 by default.

For commands that act as the owner, set a current access token issued for that owner by the configured issuer. The CLI reads it from the environment or a file and never prints it or accepts it as a command-line value:

export ASTRAL_OWNER_TOKEN="<current owner access token>"
astralvessel check
astralvessel ask "hello"
astralvessel conformance

See CLI token handling and pairing.

docs.title: Stop the node
docs.text:
astralvessel down

down --volumes also deletes the node's data, including its signing key.

docs.title: CLI
docs.text: Command Does astralvessel up Writes a deployment if there is none, writes Compose, starts the containers, waits, runs the probes and the node checks. astralvessel check Runs the isolation probes and the node checks again. astralvessel conformance Runs the acceptance checks against the running node. astralvessel pair Prints the node's pairing code and payload. --executor prints the executor's. astralvessel ask QUESTION Sends one question to the node over A2A and prints the answer. astralvessel chat Starts a conversation with the node. Press Ctrl-D to stop. astralvessel down Stops the deployment. --volumes also deletes the data volumes. astralvessel deploy FILE Writes the Compose file and prints the start command. --up starts it. astralvessel executor Runs the executor. Used inside its container. astralvessel sandbox PACKAGE Runs one sandbox. Used inside its container.

docs.title: up
docs.text:
Option Meaning --issuer URL The owner's OIDC issuer. --client-id ID The client id the owner's apps sign in with. --subject SUB Bind the node to this subject now. --image REF The node image. --port N The local port to publish. Default 8001. --upstream-url URL, --api-key env:NAME Add the model gateway. --example Add the example agent. --agent FOLDER, --mount AGENT:/TARGET=FOLDER Add an agent and its data. --timeout SECONDS How long to wait. Default 300.

These options only apply when deployment.toml does not exist yet. With a terminal, up asks for the issuer and client id it is missing.

docs.title: The owner's token
docs.text: pair, ask, chat and conformance read an access token for the owner from ASTRAL_OWNER_TOKEN, or from the file named by --token-file. They never print it.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: up exits non-zero when the node or a sandbox is not ready, or when a probe or node check fails. check and conformance exit 1 on any failure.

docs.title: Configuration tables
docs.text: Every field of vessel.toml, declared tool files and deployment.toml, with its type, default and constraints. These tables are generated from AstralVessel's pydantic models when the site is built. Unknown keys are refused in every table. For what each setting does, see vessel.toml and deployment.toml.

docs.title: Manifest
docs.text:
The top level of vessel.toml.

Field Type Default Constraints agent AgentSection required tools ToolsSection table below sandbox SandboxSection table below output OutputSection table below

docs.title: AgentSection
docs.text:
[agent]

Field Type Default Constraints name str required matches ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,62}$ description str required version str "0.1.0"

docs.title: ToolsSection
docs.text:
[tools]

Field Type Default Constraints builtin list[str] [] declared list[str] []

Also checked when the file loads:

  • Every builtin entry must be one of read, grep, glob, list, bash.

docs.title: SandboxSection
docs.text:
[sandbox]

Field Type Default Constraints workdir str "/workspace" mounts list[Mount] [] deadline_seconds int 600 >= 5, <= 3600 tool_timeout_seconds int 60 >= 1, <= 600 tool_output_chars int 20000 >= 1000, <= 200000 dockerfile str | None none

Also checked when the file loads:

  • dockerfile must be inside the agent folder.

docs.title: Mount
docs.text:
An entry of [sandbox] mounts.

Field Type Default Constraints source str required target str required read_only bool true

docs.title: OutputSection
docs.text:
[output]

Field Type Default Constraints files list["png" | "svg" | "csv" | "pdf"] []

docs.title: DeclaredTool
docs.text:
Field Type Default Constraints name str required matches ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,62}$ description str required command list[str] required min length 1 parameters dict[str, Any] {"type": "object", "properties": {}} timeout_seconds int | None none input "json-stdin" | "args" "json-stdin" scope "tools:read" | "tools:search" | "tools:files" | "tools:write" | "tools:system" | "tools:execute" "tools:read"

Also checked when the file loads:

  • command needs at least one element.
  • The name may not repeat another declared tool or a built-in tool.

docs.title: DeploymentFile
docs.text:
The top level of deployment.toml.

Field Type Default Constraints node NodeSection table below owner OwnerSection required egress EgressSection table below executor ExecutorSection table below agents list[AgentEntry] []

Also checked when the file loads:

  • Agent ids are unique.

docs.title: EgressSection
docs.text:
[egress]

Field Type Default Constraints upstream_url str | None none upstream_key str "env:VESSEL_UPSTREAM_MODEL_KEY"

Also checked when the file loads:

  • upstream_url, when set, must be an http:// or https:// URL with a host and no spaces, or env:NAME with a valid variable name.

docs.title: NodeSection
docs.text:
[node]

Field Type Default Constraints project str "astralvessel" matches ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,62}$ image str "astralvessel-node:local" matches ^[^\s]+$ bind str "127.0.0.1" port int 8001 >= 1, <= 65535 public_url str | None none environment dict[str, str] {} front_subnet str "172.31.247.0/24" front_address str "172.31.247.10"

Also checked when the file loads:

  • front_address must be inside front_subnet, and front_subnet must be a network address (172.31.247.0/24, not 172.31.247.1/24).
  • front_subnet must be a /28 or larger, and front_address must be in its lower half; other containers on front get addresses from the upper half.
  • public_url must be an http:// or https:// origin with no path.
  • environment names must be upper case, may not be set by the deployment itself and may not look like secrets.

docs.title: OwnerSection
docs.text:
[owner]

Field Type Default Constraints issuer str required client_id str required min length 1 subject str | None none min length 1 allowed_azp list[str] [] accepted_issuers list[str] []

Also checked when the file loads:

  • Every issuer must be an http:// or https:// URL with a host and no commas or spaces.

docs.title: ExecutorSection
docs.text:
[executor]

Field Type Default Constraints kernel_artifacts str | None none

docs.title: AgentEntry
docs.text:
[[agents]]

Field Type Default Constraints id str required matches ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,62}$ package str required sandbox SandboxProfile table below

docs.title: SandboxProfile
docs.text:
[agents.sandbox]

Field Type Default Constraints mounts list[MountGrant] [] memory str "2g" cpus float 2 > 0 pids int 512 >= 32 scratch str "256m" turn_disk str | None none user_disk str | None none

Also checked when the file loads:

  • Each mount must be read-only, and the targets must match the agent's [sandbox] mounts exactly.
  • turn_disk defaults to a quarter of scratch and user_disk to half; sizes look like 64m or 2g, and 0 < turn_disk <= user_disk <= scratch.

docs.title: MountGrant
docs.text:
An entry of [agents.sandbox] mounts.

Field Type Default Constraints target str required source str required read_only bool true

docs.title: Limits
docs.text: Limit Value Set by Tool output returned by the executor 20000 characters by default, 1000 to 200000 tool_output_chars in the agent's [sandbox] Tool call time 60 seconds by default, 1 to 600 tool_timeout_seconds Turn deadline 600 seconds by default, 5 to 3600 deadline_seconds Files a call may return 4 per call, types listed in [output] files The manifest Disk per turn and per user A quarter and a half of scratch turn_disk and user_disk Open files in a call 4096 The sandbox Tickets remembered against replay 65536 live ids, each kept 3600 seconds, in a file VESSEL_REPLAY_RETENTION_SECONDS Pairing offer life 10 minutes The node

docs.title: deployment.toml
docs.text: deployment.toml says which node to run, who owns it, and which agents the executor serves. astralvessel up writes one when there is none. Unknown keys are refused. Types and defaults are generated in Configuration tables.

docs.title: A complete example
docs.text:
[node]
project = "mynode"
image = "astralvessel-node:local"
port = 8001
public_url = "https://node.example.com"
front_subnet = "172.31.247.0/24"
front_address = "172.31.247.10"

[node.environment]
EXTERNAL_AGENT_ALLOWED_PRIVATE_HOSTS = "model.internal"

[owner]
issuer = "https://keycloak.example.com/realms/astral"
client_id = "astral-app"
subject = "the-owners-subject"

[egress]
upstream_url = "https://api.example.com/v1"
upstream_key = "env:VESSEL_UPSTREAM_MODEL_KEY"

[executor]
kernel_artifacts = "kernel-artifacts"

[[agents]]
id = "field-guide"
package = "agents/field-guide"
[agents.sandbox]
mounts = [{ target = "/data", source = "data" }]
memory = "1g"
scratch = "64m"

docs.title: [node]
docs.text:
Key Meaning project The Compose project name. Two deployments on one host need different names. image The AstralDeep node image. Default astralvessel-node:local. bind, port Where the node is published on the host. Default 127.0.0.1:8001. public_url The origin devices use to reach the node. Sets PUBLIC_BASE_URL. environment Extra settings for the node, as plain NAME = "value" pairs. Names the deployment sets itself, and names that look like secrets, are refused. front_subnet, front_address The internal network the node and executor share, and the executor's fixed address.

The node always runs the personal profile with SQLite in its data volume. There is no setting for PostgreSQL.

docs.title: [owner]
docs.text: Key Meaning issuer The OIDC issuer the node trusts. client_id The client id the owner's apps sign in with. subject Binds the node to this subject now. Without it the first owner whose token verifies binds the node. allowed_azp More client ids whose tokens the node accepts. accepted_issuers More issuers.

docs.title: [egress]
docs.text: Optional. See The egress.

docs.title: [executor]
docs.text: kernel_artifacts names a folder with the pinned kernel wheel and mailbox binary for the build architecture. It is passed to the image build, which checks both sha256 values against config/kernel-binding.json and fails if either artifact is missing or differs. A checkout needs it. A deployment that uses the released images does not.

docs.title: [[agents]]
docs.text:
Key Meaning id Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. Names the agent and its sandbox. package The agent folder, relative to this file. sandbox Limits and the data the sandbox may read. See below.

A deployment may have no agents. The node then runs alone.

docs.title: [agents.sandbox]
docs.text: Key Meaning mounts Data folders for the agent, read-only. They must match what vessel.toml declares. A source is a path, env:NAME or volume:NAME. memory, cpus, pids Container limits. scratch Size of the scratch filesystem. turn_disk, user_disk Disk a turn and one user may hold inside scratch. A quarter and half of scratch by default.

docs.title: env: values
docs.text: A value of the form env:NAME stays a reference that Compose fills from the environment or .env. The secret is never copied into the Compose file.

docs.title: Check a file
docs.text: astralvessel deploy deployment.toml loads the file, refuses a deployment whose grants do not match its agents, and writes the Compose file.

docs.title: The executor
docs.text: The executor runs a tool only after it has verified a ticket. It sits between the node and the sandboxes and listens only on the front network, so no sandbox can reach it.

docs.title: The interface
docs.text:
All routes except /health need Authorization: Bearer <token>. Two kinds of token exist, both derived from VESSEL_SANDBOX_TOKEN.

  • The operator token is in .generated/executor.env. It lists the catalog and asks for the pairing offer. It cannot run or end a call (executor.token_scope).
  • Each agent has its own token, listed in .generated/executor-agents.json. It runs and ends calls for that agent only. It lists only that agent's tools. A call that names another agent gets executor.token_agent_mismatch.
Route Does GET /health Reports each sandbox's confinement and the executor's mesh state. GET /tools Lists each agent's tools with schema, scope and definition hash. GET /pairing Offers the executor's pairing code and payload to the owner. POST /run Verifies a call and runs it. POST /end Ends a turn and removes its workspace.

POST /run takes agent, tool, arguments_json, action_json, ticket_json, workspace and owner.

The generated Compose file points the node at the executor with ASTRAL_VESSEL_EXECUTOR_URL. The node gets the operator token in ASTRAL_VESSEL_EXECUTOR_TOKEN, from .generated/node-executor.env, which up rewrites each time. It reads the agent tokens from /run/secrets/executor-agents.json, named by ASTRAL_VESSEL_EXECUTOR_AGENT_TOKENS_FILE. A deployment with no agents sets none of these.

docs.title: What it checks, in order
docs.text:
1. The tool exists for that agent. Otherwise executor.tool_unknown.
  2. The action names the same tool and the digest of exactly these arguments. Otherwise request.call_mismatch.
  3. The action's tool_def equals the executor's own definition hash. Otherwise gate.tool_def_changed.
  4. The kernel verifies the ticket offline, with the effect kind taken from the tool's scope. Otherwise a ticket.* or gate.* code.
  5. The verified mesh, device and turn equal the action's, and the ticket's last agent is the action's agent. Otherwise ticket.unauthorized.
  6. The ticket's mesh is the executor's own mesh. Otherwise ticket.wrong_mesh.
  7. The deployment names its owner (subject in [owner]). Otherwise executor.owner_unbound.
  8. An owner or workspace in the request equals the derived one. Otherwise request.call_mismatch.
  9. This ticket has not run before. Otherwise ticket.replayed.

The kernel's action has nine fixed fields and no owner or workspace, so a ticket cannot carry them. The executor never takes them from the request. The owner is the deployment's configured owner, bound to the mesh the ticket proves. The workspace is derived from the verified mesh and turn, and /run returns it so the node can end the turn. The agent is bound by the definition hash. It is the kernel's hash of the tool's name, description, input schema and annotations, with {"agent": "<id>"} added to the annotations. A tool published to the mesh with that annotation carries that hash in the ticket.

Every refusal returns HTTP 403 with a dotted code, and nothing runs.

docs.title: Replay memory
docs.text: The executor writes each ticket's id to spent.db in its data volume before the tool runs, so a restart cannot replay a ticket. An id is kept for VESSEL_REPLAY_RETENTION_SECONDS (default 3600), which must be longer than the longest ticket life the owner's devices mint. The kernel's default is 300 seconds. The file holds at most 65536 live ids. When it is full the executor answers HTTP 429 with executor.replay_memory_full and runs nothing, rather than forget an id.

docs.title: Joining the mesh
docs.text:
The executor waits until the node has joined the owner's mesh. Then it opens its own kernel through the node's mailbox and offers pairing. Until the owner approves, /health shows not_enrolled and every call is refused with executor.not_enrolled.

astralvessel pair --executor

The image build fails unless the pinned kernel wheel is present and has the pinned sha256. If the binding still cannot be imported at run time, the executor refuses every ticket and every pairing offer with executor.no_kernel. That code is never used for a transport failure, which Deep reports as executor.unavailable.

docs.title: Revoking access
docs.text: Revoking a tool's grant on the owner's device stops new tickets for it. A ticket already minted stays valid until it expires, because the executor checks it offline. A stop on the mesh cuts every outstanding ticket at once. The executor refuses it with a ticket.* or gate.* code after the stop syncs.

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• The executor syncs through the node's mailbox. It needs a route to it on front. It has no relay, so it reaches the mailbox only by its direct addresses.
  • The node-side adapter that sends calls to POST /run is not part of AstralVessel.

docs.title: Migration from 0.6.0
docs.text: 0.6.0 was an agent server. This release is the base's headless installation. Read this page before you upgrade.

docs.title: What was removed
docs.text:
• The agent loop, the model client, the A2A server and the Python client for it.
  • The app key, issuer and X-Vessel-User identity model. The node's owner token takes its place.
  • The task store, the app-side history store and the transcript format.
  • Service tools, web tools (webfetch, websearch), the SearXNG search container and the rich-output tool.
  • prompt.md, the [model] table and [output] primitives in vessel.toml.
  • astralvessel serve, astralvessel client and the stress/ load tool.
  • The [vessel], [search], [[apps]], [[issuers]] and services settings in deployment.toml.

Nothing was left behind in a disabled state. If you need the old server, stay on 0.6.0.

docs.title: What replaces it
docs.text: 0.6.0 Now A2A to vessel:8700/agents/<id> A2A to the node at /a2a, served by Deep's loop App key and X-Vessel-User The owner's access token from the owner's issuer astralvessel chat AGENT astralvessel chat astralvessel ask AGENT QUESTION astralvessel ask QUESTION The vessel container The node and executor containers Tasks in vessel_data The node's SQLite database in node_data

docs.title: Convert the deployment file
docs.text:
1. Replace [vessel] with [node]. Keep project, front_subnet and front_address. Add image if you do not use the default.
  2. Add [owner] with issuer and client_id. Add subject to bind the node now.
  3. Keep [egress] only if you want the model gateway. Its upstream_url is now optional.
  4. Delete [search], every [[apps]] and [[issuers]] table, and every services table.
  5. Delete model, prompt_append and any other agent field the loader now rejects.

In each agent's vessel.toml, delete [model], examples and primitives, remove webfetch and websearch from builtin, and delete prompt.md. Service tools must be removed or rewritten as command tools.

Run astralvessel up. The loader names anything it still refuses.

docs.title: Volumes and secrets
docs.text: The old <project>_vessel_data volume is not read. Delete it when you are sure you do not need it. VESSEL_APP_KEY and VESSEL_APP_KEY_SHA256 are no longer used. VESSEL_SANDBOX_TOKEN is unchanged. The model key is still held only by the egress, and the node keeps its provider keys in the product.

docs.title: Isolation probes
docs.text: The probes now run 33 checks for the example deployment against the new containers. They check the node, the executor and the egress instead of the vessel and the search container.

docs.title: The egress
docs.text:
The egress is optional. Add it when you want the model key to stay out of the node.

[egress]
upstream_url = "https://api.example.com/v1"
upstream_key = "env:VESSEL_UPSTREAM_MODEL_KEY"

The egress is the only container that holds the key. The node joins the egress network and can call http://egress:8080/v1 with the egress token, which is derived from VESSEL_SANDBOX_TOKEN and written to .generated/egress.env. The egress refuses any caller without it.

The node's own provider settings stay in the product, where they are encrypted. The egress does not change that.

The egress also runs a filtered web proxy on port 3128. It allows only globally routable addresses on ports 80 and 443.

Without [egress] no egress container runs.

docs.title: Pairing
docs.text: Pairing adds the node to the owner's mesh. The node offers a code, and a device the owner already uses approves it.

docs.title: Print the offer
docs.text:
export ASTRAL_OWNER_TOKEN=<an access token for the owner>
astralvessel pair

The command asks the node's POST /api/node/pairing as the owner. It prints a code, a payload and the node's address. The offer expires after ten minutes. Run the command again for a new one.

If the node is already in a mesh, the command says which one and prints no code.

docs.title: Approve it
docs.text:
In the AstralDeep app on a device that is already in the mesh, choose Add a device, then enter the code or paste the payload. Approve it on that device.

When it is done, GET /api/node/descriptor shows the mesh id, the member id and the mailbox address.

docs.title: Add the executor
docs.text:
astralvessel pair --executor

This works once the node has joined. Approve the second offer the same way. See The executor.

docs.title: Who can pair
docs.text: Only the owner. The node refuses any other token with HTTP 403, and a call with no token with HTTP 401. The first owner whose token the node verifies binds the node, unless the deployment names subject in [owner].

docs.title: Several deployments on one host
docs.text:
Give each deployment its own folder, project name, front subnet and published port.

[node]
project = "second"
port = 8002
front_subnet = "172.31.248.0/24"
front_address = "172.31.248.10"

up picks a free project name, a free /24 and writes them when it creates the file. A stopped deployment keeps its volumes, so its name is not reused. Two deployments cannot share a folder because the secrets folder sits beside the Compose file.

docs.title: Which images up uses
docs.text:
Installed from Executor, sandbox and egress images PyPI The released ghcr.io/astraldeep/astralvessel:<version> and ...-egress:<version> A checkout Built locally from the checkout, tagged <project>:local and <project>-egress:local

The node image is always the one named in [node] image. AstralVessel does not build or pull it.

docs.title: Upgrade
docs.text:
pip install --upgrade astralvessel
astralvessel up

From a checkout, run git pull --ff-only and then astralvessel up. up writes the Compose file again, rebuilds and recreates what changed. A sandbox whose fingerprint does not match is not served.

To upgrade the node, build or pull a new node image, set image, and run astralvessel up. The node refuses to start if its SQLite schema does not match the revision the image pins.

docs.title: What survives
docs.text:
Kept Where The node's database, signing key and mesh keys The <project>_node_data volume The executor's mesh keys The <project>_executor_data volume The node's encryption secrets .generated/node.env. They are created once and kept. Per-container tokens Derived again from VESSEL_SANDBOX_TOKEN

Back up .generated/node.env and the data volumes together. The secrets encrypt what the node has stored.

docs.title: How releases are made
docs.text: Releases come from a version tag on main. Set version in pyproject.toml, run the Release workflow by hand for a dry run, then push the tag v<version>. Release builds pass the pinned kernel artifacts as the kernel-artifacts build context so the executor image can verify tickets.

docs.title: Isolation and probes
docs.text: This page lists the isolation each container and each tool call gets, and the probes that check it on a running deployment.

docs.title: Containers
docs.text:
Every generated container runs with a read-only root filesystem, all capabilities dropped, no-new-privileges, and limits on memory and processes.

Container Limits Can reach sandbox memory, cpus, pids and scratch from its profile. /tmp is noexec,nosuid,nodev. Only its tools-<agent> network, where only the executor answers executor 1 GB, 256 processes, 64 MB /tmp. Listens only on front. The node and every sandbox node 2048 processes. Capabilities dropped. Its root is not read-only because the node writes its own data. front and outside egress 512 MB, 128 processes The outside network

Each sandbox holds its own token, derived from the master secret, and nothing of the node.

docs.title: Each tool call
docs.text:
grep, bash and declared command tools run as separate processes. Before each one runs, it is confined:

Mechanism Effect Landlock (filesystem) Read and execute only the system directories (/usr, /bin, /sbin, /lib, /lib64, /etc, /opt), the agent folder, the workdir, the mounts, and a few devices (/dev/null, /dev/zero, /dev/urandom, /dev/random). Write only the turn's workspace. No /proc, so no view of other processes. Socket files cannot be created. Landlock (network) No TCP bind or connect. Landlock (scoping) No signals to processes outside the call, no abstract Unix sockets outside it. seccomp No SysV IPC or POSIX message queues (shared by everything running as one user), no IPv4 or IPv6 sockets. No setsid or setpgid, so every process stays in the call's session. no_new_privs Set before the rules apply. Environment Only PATH, LANG, HOME, TMPDIR and VESSEL_OUTBOX. Time and output The tool's timeout, then the whole process group is killed; output is capped (see Limits). Strays Processes a call leaves behind are killed. Files and disk At most 4,096 open files; no file larger than the turn's disk limit; disk limits per turn and per user.

If confinement cannot be applied, the call fails with exit code 126 and does not run. A sandbox whose kernel lacks Landlock ABI 6 refuses to start.

read, glob and list run in the sandbox's server process instead. They are held to the same readable paths and check where an opened file or folder really points, so links cannot lead them outside.

docs.title: Run the probes
docs.text:
astralvessel check probes a running deployment from inside its containers and prints PASS or FAIL for each claim. astralvessel up runs the same probes every time it starts a deployment.

astralvessel check

It probes every agent in the deployment, with that agent's own mounts and limits, and exits non-zero if any probe fails. Run it while the deployment is idle: a probe runs real tool calls and fills a turn's disk limit, and a user's tool call arriving meanwhile can stop a probe part way, which shows as a failure. CI runs it against the example deployment on every pull request. The scripts run inside the containers through docker compose exec, with their input on stdin, so no secret appears in a process listing.

Area Probes Sandbox network no route to the internet, cannot resolve or reach the egress, cannot reach the model host directly, cannot reach the node API or its mailbox, cannot reach another agent's sandbox Sandbox contents holds no task or conversation store, holds no node secret or model key, holds its own token and not the master, root filesystem is read-only, scratch space is noexec, every mount is read-only Tool calls a background process does not outlive its call, a call cannot read another call's scratch, cannot list processes, cannot open TCP connections, cannot create a socket file, cannot use shared memory, cannot open UDP sockets, glob cannot climb out of the agent's data Workspaces calls in one turn share its workspace, a call cannot read another turn's workspace, a turn's workspace is gone once it ends, the sandbox refuses a malformed workspace key, a turn over its disk limit is stopped and emptied Files a file written to the outbox reaches the executor, the outbox refuses other types, big files and links, an outbox swapped for a link exposes nothing Executor no direct route to the internet, refuses a caller without its token, lists what its agents may run, keeps its keys private, refuses a forged ticket with a dotted code and runs nothing, refuses a tool the agent does not offer, refuses an unknown agent Egress refuses the cloud metadata address, private addresses and shared addresses, refuses odd ports, allows a public site on 443, refuses a model call without the token

check also runs five node checks: the node reports ready, its descriptor names the owner's issuer, and its data directory, database file and signing key are private.

The example deployment with one agent runs 33 probes and 5 node checks. Each further agent adds about 25 probes. The disk limit probe is skipped, and says so, when turn_disk is too close to scratch to overfill one without filling the other.

docs.title: Platform support
docs.text:
Sandboxes depend on Linux kernel features, so where AstralVessel can run safely is decided by the host kernel. This page says what is supported and what has not been checked.

Platform Status Linux 6.12 or newer, x86_64 or arm64, with Landlock ABI 6 Supported. CI runs the tests and the isolation probes on Ubuntu 24.04 runners (x86_64). Linux older than 6.12, or with Landlock disabled Not supported. Sandboxes refuse to start. Other CPU architectures Not supported. The seccomp filter exists only for x86_64 and aarch64; elsewhere every confined call fails. macOS with Docker Desktop, Apple silicon Supported. Containers run in Docker Desktop's Linux VM, whose kernel offers Landlock ABI 6. Checked on Docker Desktop 29.5 (VM kernel 6.12) with astralvessel up --example: all isolation probes passed. Older Docker Desktop versions may ship an older kernel; the sandbox then refuses to start and up shows why. Windows with Docker Desktop Unverified. Containers run in Docker Desktop's Linux VM (WSL 2); whether its kernel offers Landlock ABI 6 has not been checked.

Released images are built for amd64 and arm64.

docs.title: Check a host
docs.text:
Landlock ABI 6 is what the sandbox checks for. Run the same check the sandbox makes, inside the AstralVessel image:

docker run --rm astralvessel:local python -c "from astralvessel import confine; print(confine.abi_version())"

It prints the kernel's Landlock ABI version; 6 or higher is required. 0 means Landlock is unavailable. If the deployment is already running, a sandbox that cannot confine exits at startup with:

this kernel lacks Landlock ABI 6; per-call isolation is unavailable (set VESSEL_UNCONFINED=1 only for development)

docs.title: Python
docs.text: The astralvessel command needs Python 3.11 or newer; CI tests 3.11 and 3.12. The executor and sandbox image uses Python 3.11, the egress image Python 3.12. The node image brings its own Python.

docs.title: Threat model
docs.text: This page says what AstralVessel assumes an attacker can do, what it protects against that, and what it leaves out of scope.

docs.title: The assumption
docs.text: The model, and everything the model reads, may be hostile. A prompt injection can make an agent try any tool it has. The worst a hijacked agent can do is bounded by what the deployment grants it and by the tickets the owner's devices mint.

docs.title: What it protects
docs.text: Asset Protection The owner's data on the node One owner per node. The node's data directory is mode 0700, and its database and keys are mode 0600. The model key Held only by the egress, when one is used. The node's API Sandboxes have no route to it. Only the owner's token and the mesh reach it. Tool effects The executor runs a tool only for a verified ticket that covers this tool, these arguments, this agent, this owner and this workspace. A ticket runs once. Agent data Mounted read-only. Writable mounts are not supported. Other users of the same agent Each tool call is confined to its own turn's workspace. See Isolation and probes. The host network The egress proxy reaches only globally routable addresses on ports 80 and 443.

docs.title: Out of scope
docs.text:
• Kernel and container escapes. Isolation rests on Landlock, seccomp and Docker.
  • What an agent says. An agent can pass anything it may read to the owner.
  • A stolen owner device before the owner removes it from the roster.
  • A roster the executor has not synced. The executor trusts the roster it last received.
  • Denial of service by someone who holds a valid ticket.

See What it trusts.

docs.title: What it trusts
docs.text:
Isolation holds only as long as the parties below behave.

Trusted party Trusted to If it misbehaves The operator Write deployment.toml, hold the secrets, choose what each agent may reach Can grant anything The host kernel Enforce Landlock, seccomp and namespaces A kernel bug can break every isolation claim Docker and Compose Enforce networks, read-only mounts and resource limits Same as the kernel The owner's issuer Sign tokens only for the real owner Can act as the owner on the node The owner's devices Hold their keys and mint tickets only for what the owner approved A stolen device can mint tickets until it is removed from the roster The node image Run Deep's gates and keep the owner's data private Sees everything the owner sends it The model provider Handle the prompts and data it receives Sees every prompt and tool result sent

docs.title: Secrets and where they live
docs.text:
Secret Held by Never reaches Model key (VESSEL_UPSTREAM_MODEL_KEY) egress node, executor, sandboxes Egress token (derived) node, egress sandboxes, executor Sandbox master (VESSEL_SANDBOX_TOKEN) executor, deploy sandboxes, node, egress Executor token (derived) executor, the node's tool adapter sandboxes Per-sandbox token (derived) executor, that sandbox other sandboxes Node encryption secrets and signing key node everything else Executor mesh keys executor everything else

Generated secrets are written to .generated/ beside the Compose file with mode 600, in a folder of mode 700 that carries its own .gitignore. Never commit .env, compose.generated.yml or .generated/.

docs.title: Development mode is not a sandbox
docs.text: VESSEL_UNCONFINED=1 lets a sandbox start without Landlock. It exists for tests. Never use it with real data.
